College football rivalry trophies , which historically began and started as the result of campus pranks, local wagers, and long-standing regional grudges, represent some of the sport's most distinctive, storied, and unique traditions. The backstories of these rivalry trophies are fascinating and deep. One of them that will be won this week is the Old Oaken Bucket that will once again be awarded to the winner of the Purdue vs. Indiana game. This classic oak well bucket was first taken from a farm in southern Indiana in 1925. The schools are connected by a chain, and the series history is recorded by adding brass "I" and "P" links to the handle after each game. picks.blurb: TCU vs Texas Tech Score Predictions From the KillerFrogs Staff Skip to main content SI.COM Frogs in the Pros FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS SI.COM FROGS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM FROGS BB MEM'RIES SWEET TCU was unable to capture a win in its home finale against #2 Utah, losing 38-17. However, the Horned Frogs will get one more shot at becoming bowl-eligible on Thanksgiving Day against the No. 9-ranked Texas Tech Red Raiders. With Sonny Dykes no longer serving as the head coach of the Frogs, interim head coach Andy Avalos will be tasked with attempting to upset Texas Tech in Lubbock. Kickoff is set for 7 p.m. CT on ESPN. The Horned Frogs enter the game at 5-6 overall and 3-5 in the Big 12. Texas Tech is 10-1 and 7-1 in conference play. If TCU pulls off the big upset on Thursday, they will become bowl-eligible. Otherwise, the Frogs' season will be over. Either way, the Frogs will have changes coming their way. Texas Tech had a narrow win last week, as Baylor took the Red Raiders to the wire before they came out on top, 20-10. If the Frogs can make Texas Tech QB Thomas Castellanos uncomfortable like Baylor did, I like the Frogs' odds. Texas Tech has also struggled with consistency this season. However, the Frogs will have their hands full if they let him dictate where the ball goes. As I wrote in my Utah report card , the Frogs have quite a bit to fix, but I truly believe they will be playing hard for Andy Avalos in the regular-season finale. Can the Horned Frogs protect the football, play hard, and bring the energy? Here’s how the KillerFrogs staff sees the regular-season finale. KillerFrogs staff prediction standings through the Utah game, entering Texas Tech week. | KillerFrogs.com Why the Staff Picked TCU or Texas Tech Why the Staff Picked TCU or Texas Tech JD Andress sees Texas Tech’s defensive front posing a major problem for the Frogs, leaving the TCU offense without many answers. Michael Bara V believes the rivalry and the interim coaching change will bring out something special in the Frogs. He expects the defense to rally behind Andy Avalos and help TCU pull off the upset. Aiden Reed sees TCU eliminating Texas Tech from Big 12 contention, assuming BYU wins, as the Frogs take advantage of having nothing to lose and fighting for bowl eligibility. He also expects TCU to pull off its annual Thanksgiving upset. Baileigh Sheffield expects the Frogs to keep things competitive early, but sees Texas Tech pulling away in the second half for a two-touchdown victory. Jackson James is counting on history repeating itself, pointing to TCU's upset of an in-state rival after its last coaching change in 2021. He believes the Frogs will do it again on Thanksgiving Day in Lubbock. Skyler Gerard expects the Frogs to have some extra fire in their regular-season finale under interim head coach Andy Avalos. He’s counting on the defense to hold up as it has all season and help TCU pull off the upset. As for me, I have been saying all season long that the Frogs would upset Texas Tech, and I'm sticking to that prediction. I believe this team has one more fight left in it, and I expect TCU to rise to the occasion in Andy Avalos' first game as interim head coach. Holmes Jr. My TCU vs. Texas Tech prediction backs the Horned Frogs +14.5 tonight, given the Red Raiders' red-zone struggles despite their overall statistical edge. TCU (5-6, 3-5 Big 12) visit No. 9 Texas Tech (10-1, 7-1) in Week 13's Battle for the Saddle on Thursday, Nov. 26, at Jones AT&T Stadium in Lubbock, Texas (8 p.m. ET, ESPN). Kalshi lists Texas Tech as a 14.5-point favorite, with a total of 47.5 points and moneyline probabilities of 87% for Texas Tech and 16% for TCU. I'm fading the double-digit favorite in my latest college football picks . Spread prediction: TCU Horned Frogs +14.5 Total prediction: Under 47.5 Prop: TCU +3.5 first quarter TOP PICK TCU vs Texas Tech spread prediction: TCU +14.5 I'm fading the move toward the Texas Tech Red Raiders now that the spread has crossed a key number. I'll take TCU Horned Frogs +14.5, down to +12.5 . The Red Raiders opened as 10.5-point favorites at Kalshi. However, the line movement feels driven more by perception than new information . TCU firing Sonny Dykes this week is a new development, but Texas Tech's statistical edge and the Horned Frogs' absence of starting quarterback Jaden Craig were already factored into the opening line . More importantly, the Red Raiders rank 77th nationally in third-down conversion rate and 108th in red-zone scoring rate . That's a problem when laying nearly two touchdowns because converting in high-leverage situations is how favorites build a margin. TCU vs Texas Tech live odds movement TCU vs Texas Tech Over/Under pick: Under 47.5 The Under 47.5 is tradable down to 45.5 . Texas Tech can overwhelm TCU, so the Horned Frogs need to turn this game into a rock fight to have any shot at an upset. The Red Raiders have the 16th-highest rushing rate in the country, and TCU's defense ranks 18th in yards per rush allowed . The Horned Frogs also have the third-best red-zone defense nationally, which could compound Texas Tech's struggles in high-leverage situations and force the Red Raiders to settle for field goals. picks.blurb: Will Texas Tech football punch its Big 12 title ticket vs TCU? Score prediction - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football CFP And Bowl Games Rodgers goes nuclear NFL on Thanksgiving NBA Cup roundup Steelers release Aaron Rodgers MLB free agency updates Will Texas Tech football punch its Big 12 title ticket vs TCU? Score prediction Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The regular season comes to an end in Galaxy Stadium for the Texas Tech football team , with TCU coming to town for a Thanksgiving showdown under the lights. There's a lot going on here, but we'll begin with TCU, which will have a new coach running things and a new quarterback running the show. Well, not entirely new. Adam Schobel took the reins against Utah after starter Jaden Craig missed the game due to injury. TCU has already ruled Craig out for this week's game, so Schobel will take snaps and try to lead the upset over Texas Tech. The 6-foot-5 sophomore had one pass attempt this season before going 15-of-31 for 106 yards and throwing two interceptions against the Utes. But this game is less about matchups and more about what's on the line. What's at stake for Texas Tech football Things are pretty simple for the Red Raiders this week. Beat the Horned Frogs and they're heading back to AT&T Stadium on Dec. 4 for the Big 12 Conference championship game against Utah, which has already clinched a spot in the title encounter. A loss to TCU does two things. First, it makes Texas Tech wait another two days to figure out if it's heading to Arlington, needing BYU to lose to Cincinnati. Second, no win over TCU and no BYU loss means Tech can pretty much kiss its College Football Playoff chances goodbye. Speaking of the CFP, this could be an important factor in Tech's inclusion this year. Texas Tech currently has the one-loss appeal that could get them into the field as an at-large bid, likely on the road to start the bracket. Losing the game would wipe that possibility out entirely. Something to consider is that Texas Tech just getting to the Big 12 title game probably wouldn't keep them safe in the CFP field regardless of the outcome in Arlington. With the 12-team CFP field expiring this year, the committee doesn't have much reason to protect the participants of conference championship games, which are fading away after this season to make way for the 24-team playoff next year. Texas Tech's J'Koby Williams runs with the ball against Arizona State during a Big 12 Conference football game, Saturday, Oct. 17, 2026, at Galaxy Stadium. The fired coach theory and TCU TCU made the move to part ways with Sonny Dykes following the team's 38-17 loss to Utah. Things haven't worked out well in Fort Worth since Dykes took the Horned Frogs to the national championship game. Despite two nine-win seasons since then, TCU has lacked consistency in a Big 12 that's been gettable with some form of success the last few years. The question for TCU becomes: will it follow the trend of firing your coach and coming out the next game with your hair on fire? TCU is the fifth power-conference team to have parted with its head coach during the 2026 season, the others being Baylor, NC State, Maryland, and Florida State. Of those four other teams switching coaches in season, three of them won their next game, two of them (Baylor and NC State) earning wins of 21 points or more. This theory doesn't always come to fruition, however. During the 2025 coaching cycle, six power-conference programs fired coaches during the season and just one of them won their next game following the axing. That one win came from Virginia Tech, which beat Wofford, so it barely counts. Score prediction for Texas Tech football vs TCU Texas Tech 34, TCU 31: TCU's staff and players are all trying to impress whoever the next head coach is, so they'll be pulling out all the stops in this one. Texas Tech has to manage that, but the home crowd gets them back to Arlington. It might get there again soon, but for now, the rivalry is in a holding pattern. Florida is 20th in the latest College Football Playoff rankings after winning two straight to turn the season back around after a rough stretch. Florida State is waiting for new head coach Glenn Schumann to start, but the Georgia defensive coordinator is still a little busy for a bit at his current gig. He's on the way, but for now, the Seminoles can close the season strong with a win over the Gators and become bowl eligible. Win this, and it'll be the program's first eight-win regular season since 2020, when the Gators played for the SEC title. Florida State has played well under interim head coach Rick Stockstill, but when it had a chance for a sixth win and bowl eligibility, it lost to NC State 28-10 last week. It gets one more shot. Florida has won five of the last seven in the series. The passing game is dangerous, but the Noles don't win when they bomb away. They win when they get things going on the ground, going 4-1 when running for 175 yards or more. It's possible to run on the Gators, but Florida State isn't Georgia, or even Missouri, when it comes to being able to grind. And then there's the other side. Florida is 7-0 when running for more than 120 yards. Run well on the Noles, beat the Noles. Why Florida State Will Win Everyone wants to win a rivalry game like this, and of course Florida will bring the full focus, but this is existential for the Seminoles. It'll be iffy whether or not the program would want to accept a bowl invite, or be able to, considering the regime change, but this is for six wins. This is for a bowl game. Florida's defense isn't bad, but it doesn't come up with enough third down stops. Florida State has to control the positive momentum from the start. It doesn't need big plays, but with its tempo, it has to keep the Gators on their heels with a good offensive balance. Florida vs Florida State Prediction, Betting Lines This should be fun. There's a new energy around the Florida State program, the team will come up with a strong first quarter, and then the Gator offense will start to take over. It might not start working right away, but Florida's offense will keep steadily producing. The flash might not be there, but it won't need to be. Kickoff is scheduled for 3:30 p.m. and will be televised on the ACCN. FSU will celebrate its annual Homecoming and Seminole Heritage game and will wear turquoise jerseys and pants for the first time in program history. FSU is 3-0 in Heritage games and 63-12-1 all-time on Homecoming, with 12 consecutive victories. Throughout Native American communities, turquoise represents harmony, friendship and fellowship. The team found out it would wear the jerseys Sunday when defensive back Zae Thomas, a member of the Seminole Tribe of Florida, displayed the uniforms in the team meeting. For more information on FSU's unique relationship with the Seminole Tribe of Florida and Seminole Heritage, visit noles.co/Heritage. Florida State (5-5, 3-4 ACC) and NC State will meet for the 45th time, with the Noles leading the series, 27-17, including a 16-6 record in Doak. However, NC State has won the last four matchups with Florida State and six of the last seven meetings. Last year, the 11-21 loss at NC State likely cost the 5-win Seminoles the opportunity to become bowl eligible. Under interim head coach Rick Stockstill, the Seminoles will attempt to win their third consecutive game before closing out the season against the Florida Gators at home on Black Friday afternoon, again with another short week to prepare. The last time FSU won 3 straight games was to open the 2025 season before then losing 7 of the next 9 games. The Wolfpack (4-6, 2-5 ACC) also fired their head coach, Dave Doeren, midseason, ending his 14-year tenure as the winningest coach in Wolfpack history, compiling a 98-74 overall record, including 11 bowl appearances and 10 winning seasons. Former NFL quarterback and former Chuck Amato-coached NC State alum, Phillip Rivers, bringing six years' experience as a Catholic high school football head coach, was officially hired as the new head coach for NC State earlier this week, effective next season. It has been reported that he will travel to Tallahassee along with the Wolfpack team. Rivers signed a reported five-year deal starting at $3.25 million in total compensation for his first year ($2.4375 million base salary plus $812,500 in supplemental income). This is roughly half of Doeren's previous $6.375 million salary, making Rivers one of the lowest-paid Power 4 coaches. NC State's interim head coach Todd Goebbel led the team to a 31–10 win over California before suffering a 41–3 blowout loss to Duke and a 34–31 collapse against Syracuse, where the Wolfpack blew an 11-point lead in the final five minutes. Junior 6'6" quarterback CJ Bailey Jr. has completed 186 of his 295 passes attempted for 2,289 yards with 14 TDs and 5 interceptions. Sophomore quarterback Will Wilson, who has only completed 9 of 12 passes for 35 yards, has scored 8 rushing touchdowns for the Wolfpack during his time behind center despite NC State starting seven different lineup combinations on the offensive line in their 10 games due to injuries. Sophomore running back Jayden "Duke" Scott leads the team in rushing with 504 yards on 81 attempts for a 6.22 yard/rush average, along with 5 touchdowns. On defense, linebacker Popo Aguirre leads the team in tackles with 85, followed by CB Brian Nelson II with 47. LB Elijah Satchell leads the team in sacks with five. In their last outing, FSU wrapped up their road schedule with arguably their best defensive performance of the season so far, a 16-10 win at Pittsburgh, under interim defensive coordinator Ernie Sims. FSU's defense held Pitt, previously ranked 24th in total offense (446), to just 306 total yards, or 140 yards below their season average. The Noles defense allowed only 10 points to the Panthers, 22 points fewer than Pitt's season average of 31.9 points/game, forced a crucial fourth-and-one turnover on downs in the third quarter, deflected six passes, recorded an interception, and sealed the game with a 4th-down stop on Pitt's final drive. He is the only active kicker (min. 15 attempts) in any NCAA division who is perfect in his career, and his 26 consecutive made field goals at the NCAA level is the longest active streak. Panikowski accounted for 23 points in the two road wins. He became the first FBS player since 2023 with a touchdown, field goal, and 4+ extra points in the win at BC before kicking a season-high three field goals at Pitt. His 47-yarder against Pitt was a season-long. FSU TE Corbyn Fordham is the younger brother of NC State linebacker Caden Fordham, who played against FSU in 2025 and recorded 15 tackles for NC State. NC State was the first team to defeat Florida State at Doak after the Seminoles joined the ACC in 1992. Turning our attention to Saturday, it is hard not to see the Seminoles as a bit of a vibes pick right now. Even though Florida State faced the Panthers' third-string QB, a road win after a short week will do wonders for this team's confidence. picks.blurb: Staff Predictions: Seminoles vs. No. 20 Gators | Tomahawk Nation Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Florida State Seminoles Community Tomahawk Nation November 27, 2026 Tomahawk Nation Notifications Notifications The Feed Betting Betting News FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Florida State Football Odds Florida State Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Betting Expand Betting News Community Guidelines All communities Notifications Florida State Football Happy Thanksgiving, Seminole Nation The Florida State Seminoles will attempt to become bowl-eligible for the first time since 2023 and finish their 2026 regular season at .500 when they host in-state rival Florida Gators at Doak Campbell Stadium on Friday afternoon. Kickoff is scheduled for 3:30 p.m. and will be televised on ABC. Florida State (5-6, 3-5 ACC) and Florida (7-4, 5-4 SEC) will meet for the 70th time, with Florida leading the all-time series 39-28-2, and winners of the last two matchups (40-21 in 2025 and 31-11 in 2024). FSU is 2-0 against the Gators on Fridays, winning 27-16 in 1979 and 45-38 in 2022, and the Noles have beaten five ranked SEC teams in the regular season since 2015, the most nationally among non-SEC programs. The Seminoles have started four running backs this season, including junior Zay Parks last week against NC State. Parks began his career as a walk-on and combined for 65 yards on 17 carries against Pitt and NC State, including a 9-yard touchdown on his first carry against the Wolfpack, FSU’s lone touchdown in the game. It was his second career touchdown. Meanwhile, on the Gators’ first possession Friday, running back Jadan Baugh will likely break the 1,000-yard mark for the season. Baugh already has 980 yards this season and averages 5.0 yards per carry. Baugh has recorded 8 explosive runs of 20+ yards, including runs of 75, 61, and 53 yards, and has scored 16 rushing TDs this season. UF’s Aaron Philo has firmly established himself as the starting quarterback after alternating with Tramell Jones Jr. earlier in the year. Philo enters on a two-game winning streak following victories over No. 11 Kentucky and Vanderbilt, where he completed 20 of 26 passes for 241 yards with no interceptions and added 73 rushing yards with two touchdowns. Receivers Bailey Stockton and Dallas Wilson are tied with 41 receptions each and a combined 5 receiving TDs. UF’s defense is led by linebacker Myles Graham, son of former NFL running back Earnest Graham, who leads the team with 88 tackles, 4.5 sacks, and 5.5 tackles for loss and returned a fumble 57 yards for a touchdown in last week’s win over Vanderbilt. Some other defensive players whose names we will hear mentioned are LB Aaron Chiles and DE Jayden Woods, who leads the team with 7 sacks and 11 tackles for loss. Last week against NC State, after marching 75 yards in 5 plays on their opening drive to score a touchdown, the Seminoles would only score a field goal in the second quarter, then were shut down and shut out in the second half. FSU was held to 283 total yards, lost the time-of-possession battle by over 13 minutes, and the defense gave up 464 total yards and almost 6 yards per play. Florida State shut out in the second half as Noles fall to NC State One of the few bright spots this season has been FSU kicker Gabe Panikowski, who is 27-for-27 on field goal attempts in his NCAA career, including 12-for-12 this season. He is the only active kicker (min. 15 attempts) in any NCAA division who is perfect in his career, and his 27 consecutive made field goals at the NCAA level is the longest active streak. Last week against NCST, Panikowski connected on a 54-yard field goal, the 7th-longest in FSU history. Florida State vs Florida head-to-head stats comparison Florida State is currently trending as a 6.5-point underdog with the over/under set at 53.5 points, according to FanDuel. 2026 FSU Schedule Preview: Florida Gators Read what your TOMAHAWK NATION PROGNOSTICATORS think about this Saturday’s showdown. Then look over and digest all the FREE PRE-GAME CONTENT we’ve posted leading up to this game. We would love to hear your thoughts about how you feel about this game and your final score prediction in the comments. NoleThruandThru (season record: 8-3) As much as I’d love to see a win over those slimy lizards, I’m not going to be fooled again by FSU. At least we had an amazing kicker. An end to 2026 brings a glorious beginning to 2027 and beyond with a whoooooole lot of new faces on and off the field. Go Noles forever and forever and thanks for some fun memories, Stock! UF 31, FSU 20 Jacob Smith (season record: 6-5) It’s come down to this, yet again. This is the second year in a row that game number 12 will decide whether this team makes it to a low to mid-tier bowl game. Florida State’s defense is below average, while UF’s offense is above average. On the other hand, UF’s defense is below average, while FSU’s offense is above average. This could genuinely be the second-highest scoring game of the year. Though, I think UF takes it down the stretch because of all of the injuries on defense the Seminoles are dealing with. If I’m wrong, great! I look forward to playing in the Hot Sauce Bowl presented by Frank. Florida 48, FSU 35 Seminole Uprising (season record: 7-4) It is the dawn of a new day in Tallahassee with the hiring of Glenn Schumann this week. But, as the saying goes, it is always darkest before dawn. One last time, we have to experience the Mike Norvell era as the injury-riddled Seminoles take on Florida. Two weeks ago, after beating Pitt, I would have said FSU had a chance, but the NCSU game was so bad that it is hard to find the reasons why. Florida will run the ball down Florida State’s throats for the second year in a row, and the offense is not designed to play from behind or explosive enough to take advantage of the Gators’ coverage busts on the back end. For the second year in a row, the Seminoles go 5-7. UF 31, FSU 17 Jon Marchant (season record: 7-4 ) I think it’s safe to say the temporary bump from firing Mike Norvell has won off, and along with all of the injuries on offense this team is a shell of whatever it was earlier this season. The Norvell era wasn’t all bad but there was a lot of bad, and it never quite turned out the way we all wanted it too, Norvell included. I think they’ll play harder in this one similar to how they did vs Miami, but the injuries on offense will probably be too much to overcome. Again though, if there’s any takeaway from the Mike Norvell era it’s that any result, good or bad, was never off the table. Florida 31, FSU 23 Tim Scribble (season record: 7-4 ) I fear that this week’s game will be similar to last year’s result. The Florida State defense will be unable to stop UF running back Jadan Baugh. Expect a lot of yards on the ground for the Gators to officially close the Mike Norvell era. UF 35, FSU 20 Matt Minnick (season record: 7-4, ATS: 7-4) Man, I am so tired of losing rivalry games. I just don’t see how FSU will get UF off the field on third downs. And with so many injuries on offense, I don’t see how FSU will score beyond a random explosive play. The only way FSU hangs tough is by winning the turnover battle by a big margin, and that’s tough to do when your QB leads the country in INTs. UF 35, FSU 16 Curt Weiler (season record: 7-4, ATS: 3-8) Hard to shake my belief that this will be the third time in six years Florida denies FSU a bowl bid. The Gators haven’t been an incredible team all season but their highs have been much higher than Florida State’s. Florida 31, Florida State 20 Frank DNole (season record: 5-6) If you look at the Florida State vs. Florida head-to-head comparison chart above, you will notice that the Gators hold the statistical advantage over the Noles in almost every category. Normally, that might be the recipe for a Seminole defeat. However, this week we experienced a full moon that is now in the waning gibbous phase. Not only was it a full moon, but it was also a supermoon, and most importantly, it was a Full Beaver Moon (look it up). What all this means is that the Seminoles will win the offensive, defensive, and special-teams battles because the FSU players will give 115% more effort, they will want it more, and the Noles will play with more heart than their more talented turdly opponent. FSU Seminoles 34, FFFFF 31 P erry Kostidakis (season record: 6-5, 5-6 ATS) I really can’t tell you why I’m going with this choice other than pure delusion, but I have a weird feeling about this game. Here’s a fun fact: interim coaches have gone 3-1 in the series since 2017 (well, I guess technically 3-2, since the 2017 matchup was a matchup of two interims). Two of those wins were on the UF end, but if we’re talking delusion, why not warp some stats in favor of the home team? FSU has shed two streaks (last road win, last Friday win) that were defined by a win over the Gators this season since Rick Stockstill took over, so in the interest of the rule of threes, why not finally earn bowl eligibility with a season-ending victory over the boys from Hogtown? Again, this is a feeling borne out of nothing other than an inkling, since everything on paper and on film says UF should win this one with no issues. Jaden Baugh seems to take particular joy in the rivalry, which doesn’t bode well for an FSU defense that struggles against a lot, but especially against the run. FSU is stumbling in this health-wise, the high-flying feelings of go 2-0 to the Norvell era seemingly washed away by NC State. And unless Tre Wisner has made a turnaround on being healthy, Florida State is going to have to win this on the arm of Ashton Daniels, which the cope glass-half-full way of looking at it is that he has a penchant for performing in rivalry matchups. The only non-delusional, non-anything-can-happen-in-a-rivalry-game reasons I have for thinking that FSU is capable of pulling off a win is that 1) UF has played down to its opponents all season long and 2) the Gators are vulnerable on defense, especially through the air. But brother, it’s Turkey Day, and if there’s one thing I’m thankful for, it’s me never, ever, ever, ever, ever learning my lesson. It was on 3 DEC 1977, on a snowy television at one of my MANY childhood homes; my dad was in the Army, and we lived near Choctawhatchee Beach between Niceville and Freeport, FL. We had to turn our antenna with a pair of channel locks to bring in one of three available channels. I came across this game, and being in love with football at that age, I kept the channel tuned. I was a big Steelers fan then and was more inclined to the NFL. BUT this is when I REALLY became aware of college football. Of course, I noticed those gold helmets with the Spears on the side and immediately fell in love with Florida State. The Noles went on to win that game in Hogtown 37-9, and it was their first win in the series in a decade. I was hooked. I graduated from my beloved university, and my last game as an actual student was the “Choke at Doak”. Friends and I had the opportunity to complete the victory and attend the “5th Quarter in the French Quarter” Sugar Bowl before I went off to my own 22-year Army career. But I digress… Aside from the loss to NCST, this past week has been a GREAT week for FSU generally and the football program specifically. Florida will control the game on the ground and force a takeaway or two on defense to take its third straight the series and second straight in Tallahassee. Florida football vs FSU key matchup Florida State RB Jadan Baugh vs FSU front seven : Baugh rushed for 266 yards and 2 TDs against the Seminoles and could have another big day against an FSU run defense that's allowing 171.0 yards per game. home.headline: How Brown's Season-Ending Injury Impacts Florida vs. Florida State
home.blurb: Florida hasn't lost to FSU since its horrific 5-7 season in 2023 when the Seminoles were a perfect 13-0 but still missed out on the College Football Playoffs. How Brown's Season-Ending Injury Impacts Florida vs. Florida State - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF How Brown's Season-Ending Injury Impacts Florida vs. Florida State (IMAGN Images via Reuters Connect) Jordon Lawrenz · Roundtable Sports Wed, November 25, 2026 at 12:00 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads As of Tuesday, Nov. 24, the Florida Gators officially shut down wide receiver Vernell Brown III for the rest of the season. This is news that came as no surprise , and it's crazy to see it take as long as it did. Brown had only suited up for four games this season, but he continued to appear on injury reports leading up to Florida's 34-27 win against Vanderbilt. The 7-4 Gators certainly could've used Brown in that brutal one-win stretch from Oct. 3 to Nov. 7, but at the end of the day they bounced back terrifically from Nov. 14 onward. Brown was a crucial part of this team's 4-0 start as he recorded 17 receptions for 271 yards with a pair of touchdowns. For reference, he's still third on the team in receiving yards, proving just how valuable he was during the few games when he was around. For the Gators, it's business as usual going into the final game of the year, a rivalry showdown at Florida State. Finally, Florida's offense knows it can move on once and for all without Brown. That's not a sentence they wanted to hear back on Sept. 26, but it's been a long time coming as his status had been in doubt for the better part of two months. Brown is only a sophomore, so the Gators risking further injury by putting him back on the field was never going to be the right answer. The Florida native made an immediate impact as a freshman with his 40 receptions for 512 yards. Obviously, this season took quite a turn with those losses to Missouri and South Carolina, and it doesn't feel like a coincidence that the offense scored fewer than 20 points in those games without Brown. Running back Jadan Baugh was not a factor in either of those games either, so that also didn't help the Gators chances when they lost their offensive superstar. When Brown and Baugh were both on the field, this team looked absolutely unstoppable. Now, it'll once again be up to Aaron Philo to keep this run-game going, though he looked much better through the air against the Commodores. Florida State enters this non-conference game at 5-6 overall, fighting for bowl eligibility against a Brown-less Gators offense.

Michigan's offensive futility should make it easy to go chalk with the Buckeyes . It averages the second-fewest points per game among Power 4 teams and has vacillated between starting Bryce Underwood and Tommy Carr at quarterback. But the Wolverines don't need to score much with a suffocating defense. They also have a bit of momentum after an upset of unbeaten UCLA last weekend. The vibes just seem better in Ann Arbor, which might matter the most with only bragging right at stake. Rob Oller, Columbus Dispatch: Ohio State 17, Michigan 16 : I went back and forth on this one before deciding that Michigan's offense is simply too anemic to pull off a win in Ohio Stadium. The Wolverines rank 130th in first downs, 128th in passing yards and 99th in rushing yardage per game. On the flip side, UM's defense, ranked ninth nationally, is the most reliable piece on either team, so if the Wolverines can hold OSU to 14 points they have a great chance at winning in Columbus for a third straight time. It likely comes down to which team's head and heart are into a game where the only thing on the line is bragging rights. Brianna Mac Kay, Columbus Dispatch: Ohio State 21, Michigan 17 : Ohio State's offense with Luke Fahey at quarterback has shown flashes of promise, primarily before the defense put the Buckeyes in a deficit across the past four games. If the defense can keep Michigan under its season average of 18.3 points per game, which ranks 129th in the country, the offense should be able to put together enough momentum to finish the season with a win over the Wolverines. Dan Aulbach, Columbus Dispatch: Ohio State 17, Michigan 13 : We finally get to see what happens when a stoppable force meets a moveable object. On the one hand, Michigan has the same starting quarterback as last year's edition of the rivalry, but Bryce Underwood has severely underperformed his expectations. Michigan's offense is lethargic, but Ohio State's defense has allowed 30-plus points in three of its last four games. Michigan's defense is elite (ninth in scoring defense), but so is Jeremiah Smith . The Buckeyes proved earlier in the year they can play and win against a defense-first team in Iowa, so I'll reluctantly pick the Buckeyes. picks.headline: Urban Meyer Makes Ohio State-Michigan Prediction That Buckeyes Fans Won’t Like
picks.blurb: Urban Meyer Makes Ohio State-Michigan Prediction That Buckeyes Fans Won’t Like - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football CFP And Bowl Games Rodgers goes nuclear NFL on Thanksgiving NBA Cup roundup Steelers release Aaron Rodgers MLB free agency updates Urban Meyer Makes Ohio State-Michigan Prediction That Buckeyes Fans Won’t Like Former Ohio State head coach Urban Meyer is concerned about the Buckeyes heading into their game against Michigan Getty Michael Gallagher · HEAVY Mon, November 23, 2026 at 8:25 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads ANN ARBOR, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 29: Bryce Underwood #19 of the Michigan Wolverines is pursued by Kenyatta Jackson Jr. #97 of the Ohio State Buckeyes during the fourth quarter at Michigan Stadium on November 29, 2025 in Ann Arbor, Michigan. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) Getty Ohio State head coach Ryan Day is sticking with QB Luke Fahey after losing his last two games Getty It's been a rough month for the Ohio State Buckeyes. Ohio State started 6-1 but has lost three of its last four games. The latest was Saturday's 31-28 loss at Nebraska, which officially knocked the Buckeyes out of the College Football Playoff race. All that's left now is "The Game" against the Michigan Wolverines on Saturday in Columbus. On paper, Ohio State has the better roster. Even former Buckeyes head coach Urban Meyer admits that. Meyer, who went 7-0 against Michigan during his time in Columbus, still picked Ohio State to win. However, it sounds like he wouldn't be all that surprised if Michigan ended up leaving Columbus with a win. Urban Meyer's 1 Major Michigan Concern GettyMichigan and Ohio State both head into the Big Game with serious question marks Meyer spoke on stage at an event in a video posted Sunday by 10TV Sports' Adam King, and he didn't sugarcoat where Ohio State stands. "The roster's better — Ohio State — but the best unit performing right now is the Wolverine defense. And that concerns me a little bit," Meyer said . "They really hammered UCLA. You got to think, the other side of the ball for the Wolverines is terrible — they're last in the country. And so, to still have decent numbers — only one team has over 21 points on them all year, and that was Oregon — that's a legit defense. "On offense, we got the best player in the country, maybe the best player to ever play college football — that's how good Jeremiah is. But we also have a backup quarterback, and the offensive line is not playing great. So, I think this is going to be a rock fight; a low-scoring game, and I think whoever punches the hardest is going to win the game. I expect it to be a 17-10, 17-14 game and I got the Buckeyes." The numbers back up Meyer's remarks. Michigan ranks 17th nationally in scoring defense (17.5 points per game) and ninth in total defense (278.3 yards per game). And Oregon, which beat Michigan 31-7, is the only team to score more than 21 points on the Wolverines all season. The Wolverines' defense was at its best last Saturday in an 18-16 triple-overtime upset of previously unbeaten No. 4 UCLA. Michigan held the Bruins to 187 yards through three quarters and finished with three forced turnovers and four sacks. Why Urban Meyer Expects a Rock Fight vs. Michigan GettyOhio State head coach Ryan Day is sticking with QB Luke Fahey The biggest reason for Meyer's worry is at quarterback. Starter Julian Sayin hurt his right (throwing) arm in Ohio State's 19-15 win over Indiana on Oct. 17, and he isn't expected back for Michigan. That leaves true freshman Luke Fahey under center. Fahey went 16 of 27 for 259 yards, two touchdowns, and an interception at Nebraska. But nearly all of that came early: He was 9 of 12 for 163 yards and two scores in the first half, then 7 of 15 for 96 yards after halftime. Jeremiah Smith did his part (six catches, 165 yards, two touchdowns), tying Terry Glenn's Ohio State single-season record with 17 receiving TDs. Meyer also didn't pull any punches when it came to the other side of the ball for Michigan. "That defense is legit, legit because that offense is pathetic up there. It's the worst offense in college football, yet they're in almost all the games," Meyer said . "Their defense, what they did to UCLA, was absolutely phenomenal. Our defense has been up-and-down a little bit, but their offense stinks. I see this being a very low-scoring game. This is Ohio State-Wolverine football. The toughest team is going to win this game." Michigan's offense isn't quite the worst in the country, but it's close. The Wolverines rank 131st nationally in scoring (18.3 points per game). It's quite a shift for Meyer, who reportedly called the 2026 Wolverines a "train wreck" in early October. The Buckeyes (7-4) and Wolverines (6-5) kick off at noon ET Saturday at Ohio Stadium on Fox. The Ohio State Buckeyes and Michigan Wolverines playing in Columbus on Saturday was once a game that figured to have real implications. With a combined 13-9 record between the two teams, neither has any College Football Playoff chances. It's all about the rivalry in this one. Ohio State is coming off a loss that was the nail in the coffin for its playoff hopes against Nebraska, while Michigan can feel good about a top-10 win over UCLA in three overtimes. Ahead of Saturday's game, the A to Z Sports college football staff has predictions on how this one will go in The Shoe. Ohio State 27, Michigan 17 There are jobs on the line in Columbus on Saturday, especially when it comes to Ohio State's assistant coaching staff. The defense, in particular, has to have a good showing against a bad Michigan offense after allowing 31 points against Nebraska. Ohio State's defensive issues since Week 8 have been a complete flip from the first half of the season, and it's a major reason why the Buckeyes are sitting at 7-4. Georgia (29%), Notre Dame (16%) and Texas (12%) have the best chances to win the college football national title, according to the A to Z Sports CFB Playoff Predictor (updated November 26, 2026). The Buckeyes need to send Jeremiah Smith out the right way as the best college football wide receiver of this generation. I think he'll be in store for a big game in his last appearance in Columbus and will score at least two touchdowns to solidify his Heisman case. Matt Patricia and his defense are on watch in this game. It could be his last in Columbus either way, but falling short against Michigan would all but seal his fate. I think Ohio State's offense hits enough big plays in this one to walk away with a two-score win in the end. - Brandon Little, A to Z Sports Ohio State Ohio State 27, Michigan 17. I'm taking Ohio State to beat Michigan 27-17 in a game that is much more competitive than the final score might suggest. I expect the Wolverines to make things difficult for the Buckeyes for the majority of the afternoon, keeping the game within one possession and forcing Ohio State to be patient offensively. This rivalry matchup rarely comes without some adversity, and I don't expect the Buckeyes to run away with it early. However, the difference in offensive firepower eventually becomes too much for Michigan to overcome. Ohio State starts finding more consistency in the second half, and the Buckeyes make the necessary plays down the stretch to create some separation in the fourth quarter. The biggest storyline will be Jeremiah Smith, who I think delivers a Heisman Trophy-caliber performance in what could be his final game wearing the scarlet and gray. Smith has the ability to completely change a game, and I expect him to come through with several game-changing plays when Ohio State needs them most. Whether it's winning contested catches, creating separation downfield or making something happen after the catch, Michigan will have a difficult time containing him for four quarters. Smith puts an exclamation point on his Ohio State career with a monster performance, while the Buckeyes close out another rivalry victory. - Ryan Roberts, A to Z Sports Notre Dame Ohio State 19, Michigan 12 The stakes for this game haven't been this low in a long time, but it's still the biggest game on the calendar for both teams and a matchup that's appointment television. Michigan didn't exactly get their swagger back with an 18-16 triple overtime win over UCLA, but it no doubt gave them a big boost of confidence coming into this one. Conversely, the wind has been totally sucked out of the sails of the Buckeyes after a playoff-killing 31-28 loss to Nebraska. If Michigan had ANYTHING going for them offensively, I would pick the upset. Ohio State is ripe for it. But the Wolverines are simply that bad on offense. The Buckeyes' defense keeps Michigan locked down, and Jeremiah Smith hits a couple of big shots to power the offense. - Craig Smith, A to Z Sports Miami Ohio State 33, Michigan 17 The Game, will look a little different this year. The other program is in flux yet again, with many wondering if HC Kyle Whittingham is one and done in Ann Arbor. This game being inside the Shoe only helps Ohio State. Luke Fahey hasn't played that bad, and the quarterback situation at Michigan is a mess. Give me the Buckeyes, big. - Rob Gregson, A to Z Sports Alabama Ohio State 20, Michigan 3 Things are not good in the land of the Buckeyes right now, especially after their embarrassing loss to Nebraska. And sure, it may not be a big difference between the two, but having the best player in the world should help for Ohio State. - Justin Churchill, A to Z Oklahoma This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. away.headline: Report: Michigan QB Bryce Underwood expected to be available vs. Ohio State amid injury concerns
away.blurb: Despite injury concerns following last week’s game against UCLA , Michigan quarterback Bryce Underwood is expected to be available vs. Ohio State , according to ESPN’s Pete Thamel . He was listed as questionable on the initial availability report Wednesday evening. Michigan coach Kyle Whittingham had previously announced Underwood as the starter before news broke of the lower-body injury he was dealing with out of the UCLA win. He then came in as questionable on Wednesday’s first availability report. $39.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage However, it appears Underwood will be able to go in the rivalry matchup against Ohio State on Saturday afternoon. It would be his second career start against the Buckeyes after getting the nod for last year’s game in Ann Arbor. The two teams are due to release their second availability reports Thursday evening. Underwood began this season as Michigan’s starter before Whittingham announced a change to Tommy Carr . But in light of Jason Beck’s departure as offensive coordinator, the staff opened the job back up, Whittingham previously said. Both quarterbacks played for Michigan against Oregon, and Underwood then started last week against UCLA. He went 11-for-24 for 127 yards and a touchdown, and he also completed the game-winning two-point conversion in triple overtime. “Well, like I said, last week, I believe it was, he’s handled this as well as he could possibly handle it,” Whittingham told reporters this week. “The change in quarterback, being demoted to the number two guy. Attitude never wavered. Work ethic never wavered. Preparation never wavered. He was just all-in every single day. “And I talked to him way back when the change happened. I said, ‘In this day and age of college football, odds are that you’re going to get another chance this season.’ And sure enough, he got his chance on Saturday and did a good job running the offense.” Underwood entered this season with high expectations, as did the Michigan program after Whittingham’s hiring. But as he looked back on the up-and-down nature of the year, the former top recruit said he will be better for it in the long run. “I can say the way I took this season was more of a blessing,” Underwood told reporters postgame after Michigan’s win over UCLA. “I took this as lessons being learned and everything, and how to move forward from it. “The way you can show how to be a man is facing adversity and how you take it on. That’s been my main focus these past, what, four, three, five weeks, however long. But just facing adversity, and how can I recover from it?” As a whole this season, Bryce Underwood has thrown for 1,077 yards and six touchdowns, to six interceptions, with a 54.5% completion percentage. He has also added two rushing touchdowns across nine appearances.

home.blurb: The Ohio State Buckeyes and Michigan Wolverines both have plenty to sort through on the injury front ahead of Saturday's rivalry game. Wednesday night's injury report brought some bad news for Ohio State and questionable tags for several Michigan starters, and both teams have decisions to make on who can go. Ohio State will be without linebacker Christian Alliegro. He joins quarterback Julian Sayin and running back Ja’Kobi Jackson, who had already been ruled out for the Buckeyes. Along with the players who are out, cornerback Jay Timmons and right tackle Phillip Daniels are both listed as questionable. Timmons was spotted in a walking boot after the Buckeyes' Week 12 loss to Nebraska, per multiple reports. Alliegro also had to exit early against the Cornhuskers and was unable to return. With Alliegro out, Ohio State will lean more on Riley Pettijohn, TJ Alford, and Payton Pierce. That trio will be the top three at linebacker, with freshman Cincere Johnson serving as the fourth option. The Wolverines already know JJ Buchanan will be out. On top of that, starting quarterback Bryce Underwood, running back Jordan Marshall, wide receiver Andrew Marsh, and defensive end John Henry Daley are all questionable to play against Ohio State. Daley’s status stands out on the defensive side. He's Michigan's leading sack man with eight sacks this season, and his absence would take away a big piece of the Wolverines' pass rush. If Marsh isn't able to play, Michigan would be down its top two receivers with Buchanan already out. That would put a lot on the rest of the receiver room against the Buckeyes' secondary. Ohio State has to figure out if Timmons can go, he’d be the biggest loss for the Buckeyes if he can’t. Michigan is waiting on the health of its quarterback, its No. 2 running back, a top receiver, and its best pass rusher. The final injury reports will go a long way in shaping how this rivalry game plays out to say the least. picks.blurb: Kentucky vs. Louisville game glance, opening odds, and our early prediction | A Sea Of Blue Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Kentucky Wildcats Community A Sea Of Blue November 27, 2026 A Sea Of Blue Notifications Notifications The Feed Sections Kentucky Wildcats Basketball College Basketball Recruiting Kentucky Wildcats Football College Football Recruiting Betting Betting News FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Kentucky Football Odds Kentucky Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Library Community Guidelines Media Resources Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Sections Expand Kentucky Wildcats Basketball Betting Expand Betting News Library Expand Community Guidelines Community Guidelines All communities Notifications Kentucky Wildcats Football Kentucky hopes to snap a three-game losing streak and avoid losing a third straight game to Louisville. After a great start to the season, with a 7-1 record heading into the bye week and November, Kentucky Football has now lost three straight games. The Wildcats have suffered losses to Tennessee on the road, Florida at home, and most recently Missouri on the road. Heading into the Missouri matchup, Kentucky was ranked No. 16 in the AP Top 25 Poll. However, after a 28-14 loss to the Tigers, the Wildcats have officially fallen out of the rankings. Many Kentucky fans expected the team to bounce back against Florida at home, especially with a sellout crowd at Kroger Field. Unfortunately, the Wildcats came up short on their final drive. Meanwhile, against Missouri, Kentucky had several opportunities to score more than 14 points but struggled to capitalize in the red zone. Sacks, turnovers, and turnovers on downs ultimately prevented the Wildcats from putting more points on the board. While the final three games of the season have not gone well, not many fans expected Kentucky to reach seven wins during Will Stein’s first year, especially considering the difficult schedule the Wildcats faced. Although some fans are disappointed with how the past few weeks have unfolded, many are still pleased with what Stein has accomplished during his first season. Stein has even described the year as successful, despite the possibility of losing to Louisville at home to close out the regular season. Hopefully, that will not be the case. Now, let’s get into the Louisville matchup, as they face off for the Governor’s Cup. Louisville Cardinals (8-3) Kentucky holds the all-time series lead against Louisville, 20-17, but the Wildcats have lost their last two matchups against the Cardinals. Last year, Louisville went on to win 41-0, shutting out Kentucky on the road. That result ultimately contributed to former head coach Mark Stoops being fired. In 2024, the Cardinals also defeated the Wildcats, winning 41-14 at Kroger Field in another disappointing performance for Kentucky. Before that, Kentucky won five straight games against Louisville. Now, Will Stein, who played at Louisville, is leading the Wildcats and will face his former team for the first time as Kentucky’s head coach. As for Louisville, the Cardinals got off to a rocky start, opening the season with a 2-3 record. However, they have since won six consecutive games and improved to 8-3 on the year. A major reason for Louisville’s early struggles was its defense, which had difficulty stopping opposing offenses. Meanwhile, the Cardinals’ offense continued to put up plenty of points, keeping them competitive in several games. Now, things have started to come together for head coach Jeff Brohm and his team. Louisville will look to win its third consecutive game against Kentucky and improve to 9-3 on the season. The Wildcats will certainly have their hands full, as Louisville averages 38.6 points per game, which ranks eighth in the country. The Cardinals also allow 23.4 points per game, ranking 55th nationally. Kentucky will need to find a way to slow down dual-threat quarterback Lincoln Kienholz, who has thrown for 2,739 yards while completing 67.5% of his passes. He has recorded 20 passing touchdowns and four interceptions while also contributing 392 rushing yards and 11 touchdowns on the ground. In total, Kienholz has accounted for 31 touchdowns this season, making him one of the biggest threats Kentucky will have to contain. Louisville also has two talented running backs, with Isaac Brown leading the way. Brown has recorded 120 carries for 834 rushing yards and eight touchdowns. The Cardinals also rely on Keyjuan Brown, who has totaled 96 carries for 672 yards and six touchdowns. At wide receiver, Louisville has several players who contribute to the passing game, but three have emerged as the team’s primary targets. Tre Richardson leads the group with 58 receptions for 822 receiving yards and five touchdowns. Lawayne McCoy has recorded 36 receptions for 640 yards and six touchdowns, while TreyShun Hurry has added 45 receptions for 542 yards and three touchdowns. As mentioned earlier, Louisville has not been particularly strong defensively this season, but there are a few players Kentucky will need to watch closely. Stanquan Clark leads the Cardinals in tackles with 77, making him one of the team’s most important defensive players. Kentucky will need to find ways to avoid him in space and prevent him from making plays. Defensive lineman Tyler Thompson is another player to watch, as he has recorded 6.5 of Louisville’s 32 sacks this season. That means he is responsible for roughly one-fifth of the team’s total sacks, making him a major threat along the defensive line. Kentucky will also need to take care of the football, as turnovers have become a major concern over the past three games. The Wildcats have committed turnovers in every game since their matchup against Tennessee. Kentucky recorded two fumbles and an interception against the Volunteers, one fumble against Florida, and one fumble along with two interceptions against Missouri. Those numbers are concerning, especially considering Kentucky had only five turnovers before that stretch, including three against Alabama and two against South Alabama. Louisville’s defense has recorded 12 interceptions this season, with defensive back Kaleb Beasley responsible for five of them. Kentucky will need to be especially careful when throwing in his direction. The Cardinals have also forced eight fumbles, meaning the Wildcats will need to protect the football and avoid giving Louisville any extra opportunities. If Kentucky hopes to pull off the upset, it will need to play a clean game, limit turnovers, and find a way to slow down Louisville’s explosive offense. ESPN win probability: Kentucky has just a 35.6% chance of winning, according to ESPN . Our early prediction: Before the season started, I predicted Kentucky would win six games but lose to Louisville, believing Will Stein would have too much emotion coaching against his former team, where he once played. While Kentucky is currently on a three-game losing streak and sits at 7-4 on the season, Louisville has won six straight games and is now 8-3. Many believe all the momentum is on Louisville’s side, which makes complete sense, especially since several other outlets are now predicting the Cardinals to defeat Kentucky. The Wildcats will need to finish drives and find a way to slow down Louisville’s high-powered offense. Kentucky has shown throughout the season that it can do that at times, including during matchups against South Carolina and LSU. With all of that being said, I believe this game will mirror the 2023 matchup, when Kentucky escaped with a 38-31 victory on the road. Although this year’s game will be played at Kroger Field, I believe the Wildcats will pull off another victory in a high-scoring contest. Kentucky will close out the regular season with an 8-4 record, solidifying what I believe has been a magnificent first season under Stein. Final score: Kentucky 34, Louisville 27. How Kentucky football and No. 19 Louisville match up — with a game prediction How the Kentucky Wildcats (7-4, 5-4 SEC) and the No. 19 Louisville Cardinals (8-3, 7-2 ACC) match up at each position for Saturday’s college football contest — with a game prediction: • Kentucky’s Kenny Minchey (68.1% completions, 2,448 yards, 15 touchdowns vs. four interceptions) threw one interception as UK went 7-1 in its first eight games. The Notre Dame transfer has been picked off three times, however, during the Wildcats’ current three-game losing skid. As UK played from behind in last week’s 28-14 loss at Missouri, Minchey, a 6-foot-2, 211-pound fourth-year player from Hendersonville, Tennessee, threw a season-high 43 passes, completing 27 for 288 yards with no touchdowns and two picks. • The UK defense has struggled this season against the quarterback run game and Louisville’s Lincoln Kienholz (67.5% completions, 2,739 yards, 20 touchdowns, four interceptions; 392 rushing yards, 11 touchdowns) is a more-than-capable runner. A 6-2, 215-pound junior from Pierre, South Dakota, Kienholz ran for a net-81 yards in a 44-17 win over Georgia Tech and has rushed for a net-40 yards or more in six other games. A transfer from Ohio State, Kienholz also has five games in which he has thrown for 300 yards or more, including last week’s 42-10 strafing of Pittsburgh, when he passed for 309 yards and five touchdowns vs. one interception. Advantage : Louisville Running backs • Kentucky running backs had a rough go in the loss to Missouri. UK leading rusher CJ Baxter (610 yards, 5.4 yards a carry, eight touchdowns; 13 catches, 91 yards, one TD) and backup Jason Patterson (504 yards, 5.8 yards a carry, three TDs) each left the Mizzou game early due to injuries. With Baxter and Patterson sidelined, Jovantae Barnes (347 yards, 5.1 yards a carry, three TDs) carried a season-high 16 times for 69 yards at Mizzou and scored UK’s only touchdown on a 2-yard run in the fourth quarter. Barnes also lost a fourth-quarter fumble at the Missouri 13-yard line. • Louisville’s Isaac Brown (834 rushing yards, 7 yards a carry, eight touchdowns; 19 catches, 177 yards, two touchdowns) missed last season’s Governor’s Cup rivalry game due to injury. As a freshman in 2024, Brown won the game’s Howard Schnellenberger MVP Award after carrying 26 times for 176 yards and two touchdowns in a 41-14 U of L rout of Kentucky at Kroger Field. Senior Keyjuan Brown (672 yards, 7 yards a carry, six TDs) has run for 50 yards or more in six straight games. Wide receivers • Kentucky freshman Kenny Darby (57 catches, 711 yards, three touchdowns) made eight receptions for a career-high 110 yards in the loss at Missouri. In so doing, the 6-1, 180-pound product of Bossier City, Louisiana, moved past Barion Brown (50 receptions for 628 yards in 2022) to claim UK’s freshman record for most catches and receiving yards in a season. After missing UK’s 21-14 loss to Florida two weeks ago due to injury, senior Nic Anderson (22 catches, 242 yards, one TD) returned at Mizzou and caught two passes for 19 yards. • Louisville leading receiver Tre Richardson (58 catches, 822 yards, five touchdowns) has caught 28 passes in U of L’s past four games. A 5-10, 175-pound senior from Topeka, Kansas, Richardson had a massive game against Kentucky last season while playing for Vanderbilt. In Vandy’s 45-17 decimation of UK in Nashville, Richardson caught six passes for 159 yards and three touchdowns. TreyShun Hurry (45, 452, 3) and Lawayne McCoy (36, 640, six) are also productive. • Kentucky’s Willie Rodriguez (58 catches, 560 yards, three touchdowns) caught eight passes for 93 yards in the loss at Missouri. That moved the 6-4, 249-pound, third-year player from Covington Catholic High School past Jacob Tamme (56 catches in 2007) for the most receptions in a season by a 21st Century UK tight end. Second-year player Mikkel Skinner (13, 115, 1) caught three passes for 18 yards vs. Mizzou and rushed twice for six yards. • Louisville’s Jaleel Skinner (25 catches, 362 yards, four TDs) is a cousin of UK’s Mikkel Skinner. In U of L’s 41-0 rout of Kentucky last season, Jaleel Skinner caught two passes for 21 yards and a touchdown. Advantage : Kentucky Offensive line • Kentucky right tackle Malachi Wood was knocked out of the Missouri game with an injury. UK coach Will Stein said Monday that Wood’s status to play this week is “day to day.” If the ex-Madison Central standout cannot go, left guard Olaus Alinen will shift to right tackle and Jordan Knox will move into the vacated guard spot. • Louisville left tackle Lance Robinson was named Outland Trophy National Player of the Week after earning a 90 grade with three knockdown blocks in U of L’s 44-20 romp over Florida State on Oct. 9. In that game, Robinson started at right tackle, moved to left tackle and also played a series at center. Center Evan Wibberley , played last season for Kentucky after spending his first three college campaigns at Western Kentucky. Advantage : Even Defensive line • Kentucky end Mi’Quise Humphrey-Grace (43 tackles, six sacks, 10.5 tackles for loss, nine quarterback hurries) tied for the team high with seven stops and had 1.5 tackles for loss at Missouri. After having a QB sack in three straight games against Oklahoma, Vanderbilt and Tennessee, Humphrey-Grace has gone the past two games without a sack. Tackle Tavion Gadson (39 tackles, three sacks, five TFL, two pass breakups, two fumble recoveries) made six tackles vs. Mizzou. • Louisville right defensive end Clev Lubin (49 tackles, nine sacks, 10 tackles for loss, seven QB hurries, two forced fumbles) is a disruptor. The 6-3, 260-pound Lubin had two sacks vs. UK last season. At right end, former UK player Jerod Smith II has made 20 tackles with 1.5 sacks and 4.5 TFL. Tackle Demeco Kennedy (28 tackles, one sack, three TFL) is a Frederick Douglass High School product who played with UK nose guard Jamarrion Harkless at both Douglass and then Purdue. • With 87 stops, Kentucky MLB Grant Godfrey is the second-leading tackler in the SEC. A 6-3, 240-pound fourth-year player, Godfrey has made double-digit tackles in four games this year. SLB Sam Greene (34 tackles, 1.5 sacks, two forced fumbles, an interception) made six tackles at Mizzou. • Louisville MLB Stanquan Clark (team-high 77 tackles, 1.5 sacks, seven tackles for loss, five pass breakups, 2 QB hurries) has three double-digit tackles games this season. WLB T.J. Capers (70 tackles, 1.5 sacks, four TFL, three PBU, four QB hurries) intercepted a pass in last week’s dismantling of Pitt. Capers made four tackles, two solo, vs. UK last year. Defensive backs • The Kentucky pass defense had a rough go at Missouri, giving up 314 passing yards and four touchdown throws. Cornerback Terhyon Nichols was credited with seven tackles, broke up two passes and intercepted one. Safeties Jordan Castell and Ty Bryant each have four interceptions but Castell has gone four games and Bryant three without a pick. • Louisville strong safety Kaleb Beasley is stacking his stat line. The 6-1, 200-pound third-year player from Nashville, has made 68 tackles, broken up eight passes and intercepted five. A transfer from Tennessee, Beasley had three tackles last season for UT in the Volunteers’ 56-34 win over UK at Kroger Field. Former Kentucky defensive back DJ Waller Jr. has made 17 tackles and broken up a pass. Special teams • Kentucky place-kicker Adam Zouagui is 14 of 17 on field-goal tries with a long make of 52 yards. Murray State transfer Thomas O’Hara only punted twice at Missouri, but averaged a booming 56.5 yards a kick. On the season O’Hara is averaging 42.9 yards but has pinned opponents’ inside their 20-yard line only five times on 22 kicks. Punt returner Brock Coffman , a former Louisville player, is averaging 8.9 yards on 12 returns and had a 55-yard touchdown vs. LSU. • Louisville place-kicker Carson Hilbert is 14 of 20 on field-goal tries with a long make of 54 yards. Hilbert is 6 of 12 from outside 40 yards. Punter Niall Hayes is averaging 40.2 yards and has pinned foes inside their 20-yard line only nine times on 38 kicks. Punt returner Jackson Voth is averaging 13.5 yards on 14 returns with a long of 68. Isaac Brown has averaged 23.8 yards on eight kickoff returns with a long of 71. away.blurb: Last week in the Cardinals' sluggish win over Stetson, UofL was without their starting shooting guard, Seth Trimble. Leading up to the game, reports said Trimble would miss it with a “minor injury,” and they expected him to be available Tuesday for Louisville’s matchup with Texas Tech. After gaining eligibility through the “five-for-five rule,” Trimble was one of Kelsey’s biggest additions from the Transfer Portal. He has started in every game this year, except vs. Stetson, when he was out, and with Louisville looking to pull off the upset, the UNC transfer will have to be healthy. The good news is that Trimble sounds like he will play in this huge rank-vs-rank matchup, and he is trending toward a return. He is a physical guard who will defend the opposing team’s best guard and will force turnovers, as he is averaging 1.7 steals per game, including two steals in each of the past two games. In addition to his defense, he is an offensive threat, averaging 13.3 points per game, the third-highest on the team, behind Flory Bidunga and Adrian Wooley. Trimble spent his first four seasons at North Carolina, including last season, when he averaged 14.0 points, 3.8 rebounds, 3.0 assists, and 1.3 steals per game. Clemson is now 7-4 on the season, with the team having won four of its last six games overall. The Tigers have rebounded nicely from a poor opening part of the season, despite a lackluster offense all year. But as the Tigers prepare for the final week of the regular season, the only focus is on getting a win over the rival South Carolina Gamecocks. Clemson will be hosting South Carolina in the game, giving themselves a slight edge entering the contest. South Carolina will come into the game with a record of 6-5 for the season, coming off two straight blow out losses. The Gamecocks have lost by a score of 34-6 in two straight weeks, and they will try to bounce back this week against Clemson. Both sides understand the rivalry aspect of this game, with the Tigers wanting to add another win to the season's resume. But South Carolina won't go down quietly, looking to spoil the Tigers' final home game of the year. Heading into the game, the Tigers are being viewed as the underdogs, despite having the better record than South Carolina. According to the ESPN matchup predictor , Clemson has a 44.2 percent chance of taking down the Gamecocks this week at home. Quarterback Trent Pearman will likely get the starting nod in this game after leading the Tigers to a win last week. Pearman did well enough for Clemson to win, and it seems that the program wants to see more from him in this game. Overall, Pearman went 17-of-27 for 164 yards, with no touchdown passes against the Blue Devils. But he did rush for 51 yards and a touchdown, showing that he can be a dual-threat option for Clemson. If Pearman can continue to help the offense, it could give Clemson an opportunity to grab the win. Clemson's defense has been strong all year, and South Carolina's offense has been very stagnant over the last few weeks. Clemson head coach Dabo Swinney has been criticized all season long , but if this team could get a win over the Gamecocks, it could go a long way for him. The 2026 season won't be seen as a complete success, but after how it started, the Tigers may end the year on a high note.

(Photo by David Jensen/Getty Images) Getty Zach Lentz · HEAVY Wed, November 25, 2026 at 12:52 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads CLEMSON, S.C. — The Palmetto Bowl returns to Death Valley on Saturday with pride, momentum, and a surprising betting line on the table. Despite boasting a better record and home-field advantage, the Clemson Tigers (7-4) are once again playing the underdog role. FanDuel oddsmakers have installed the South Carolina Gamecocks (6-5) as 5.5-point road favorites for the regular-season finale. The Gamecocks sit at -215 on the moneyline, while the Tigers offer +180 value. The over/under is set at a gritty 41.5 points. For the second consecutive year, both programs enter the rivalry unranked in the US LBM Coaches Poll, though Clemson quietly garnered 11 votes on Sunday. But national rankings rarely dictate the tempo of this bitter in-state clash. Clemson's Ground Game and Stifling Defense Clemson enters Saturday riding the high of a defensive masterclass. Just days ago, the Tigers walked into Durham as 13.5-point underdogs and dismantled Duke 20-10. The blueprint was simple: control the clock and suffocate the opposition. Clemson's defense allowed just 11 first downs all night, keeping the Blue Devils' offense on the field for a paltry 22 minutes and 45 seconds. By the time Duke regained possession following Chris Denson's 7-yard, fourth-quarter touchdown run, the game was effectively out of reach. Offensively, the Tigers unleashed a punishing, multi-pronged rushing attack. Three different players eclipsed the 50-yard mark, led by Jarvis Green's 84 yards on 16 carries and Denson's 71 yards. The catalyst, however, was Trent Pearman. In his first career start, the quarterback proved poised under pressure. Pearman completed 17 of 27 passes for 164 yards and added 51 yards on the ground. His decisive 9-yard touchdown scramble in the third quarter gave Clemson a lead it never relinquished. Now, he faces a South Carolina defense desperate for a bounce-back performance. Gamecocks Look to Rebound After Georgia Mauling South Carolina arrives in Death Valley needing a win to match Clemson's 7-4 record, but they must first shake off the lingering effects of a brutal 34-6 home loss to No. 1 Georgia. The Gamecocks' primary objective will be jumpstarting quarterback LaNorris Sellers. The top-ranked Bulldogs terrorized Sellers in the pocket, sacking him three times and intercepting him once. He finished the afternoon with just 87 passing yards and 24 rushing yards. If South Carolina is to cover the 5.5-point spread in one of college football's most hostile environments, Sellers will need the time and space that Georgia strictly denied him. Kickoff from Memorial Stadium is scheduled for 3 p.m. ET Saturday on ESPN2. The former Clemson football player came down with a late third-quarter interception against rivals South Carolina on Saturday night, ending a Gamecocks red-zone threat and helping top-ranked Georgia hold a 27-6 lead going into the fourth quarter. South Carolina quarterback LaNorris Sellers was driving inside the Georgia 22 when he forced a throw into traffic. Barnes was lingering and waiting. The pick took away South Carolina's best chance to cut into the deficit and handed the ball straight back to the Bulldogs. It was the only turnover of the night for either team at that point and the only one South Carolina couldn't afford at the time. The Gamecocks, ranked 21st at 6-4, had managed just two field goals before the interception. Georgia, 9-1 and ranked first, had already built a two-score cushion behind two Nate Frazier rushing touchdowns and a pair of field goals from Peyton Woodring. For Clemson fans, the sight of Barnes snuffing out a South Carolina drive had to feel familiar probably even a tad bit confusing for the head to digest. He left Death Valley, but nobody let his instincts know that they should do the same. Somewhere in Upstate South Carolina, Tigers fans are watching a former player in a Bulldogs jersey do exactly what they would have asked of him, and deciding whether to be proud or just slightly annoyed that it's happening in another uniform. Barnes may be wearing a Georgia G now, but the Tiger paw is clearly still stamped somewhere in his blood. The Gamecocks will need to regroup quickly if they are to win this one. Georgia leads 27-6 with the fourth quarter just starting up. This was written in the fourth quarter of the Georgia vs. South Carolina game.
