"You would have to be living in a cave to not understand the importance of this one," he said. Rivalry weekend is upon us, a chance to right wrongs and establish year-long bragging rights in the face of a hated opponent. Not only does this weekend's slate offer conference championship and College Football Playoff implications, but the teams out of the mix are playing for something sacred -- respect. And a few coaches are trying to keep their jobs, too. We've picked out 10 of the most important games for Week 13, beginning Thursday in Lubbock, Texas and taking us all the way to Autzen Stadium in Eugene, Oregon on Saturday night. Season results : Brad Crawford (74-37 straight up, 51-59-1 ATS); Chris Hummer (79-32 straight up, 56–54-1 ATS) After matching winning weeks, at least we fixed the radiator leak before rivalry weekend. Hummer nailed Michigan over UCLA last week, and I won with Tennessee beating LSU . I vowed to never pick Lane Kiffin again this season as a betting favorite, and it worked out for me. I'm going to need a near-perfect showing to get back to even before bowl season. Let's hope it happens. TCU at No. 11 Texas Tech (-12.5) Hummer ( Texas Tech -12.5) : You never really know how a team is going to respond following its head coach's firing. But all I know going into this one is Texas Tech is playing for everything and TCU is playing for very little. So, I lean the Red Raiders here. As for the margin … TCU's defensive front is good enough to slow Texas Tech's run game. But I also have a very hard time seeing TCU's stuck-in-the-mud offense (100th nationally in yards per play) working all that well against a Texas Tech defense that seems to have found some form the last two weeks. … Texas Tech 34, TCU 20. Crawford (Texas Tech -12.5) : This one sets up for a Texas Tech blowout as long as the Horned Frogs fail to rally under an interim coach following the firing of Sonny Dykes this week. TCU has won five of the last six in the series, but that was prior to Texas Tech's rise in the NIL era, with a roster vastly superior to most Big 12 opponents. Tommy Castellanos had his first multi-turnover game with the Red Raiders last week, so look for him to be more protective of the football en route to the program's second straight Big 12 title game appearance. ... Texas Tech 31, TCU 14. No. 25 Nebraska at No. 13 Iowa (-4.5) Hummer ( Nebraska +4.5) : These are pretty similar teams. Two top 20 squads that are at their best running the ball and when their up-and-down QBs play clean. The difference is Iowa is a bit better up front, and Nebraska's QB, Anthony Colandrea , comes with a slightly higher ceiling. I like the way Nebraska is playing of late, and I think the against-the-spread value is with the Huskers. But I also believe Iowa is the better team and far more likely to execute down the stretch in a close game. Iowa eeks by to reach 10-2. … Iowa 20, Nebraska 17. Crawford (Nebraska +4.5) : Can Huskers quarterback Anthony Colandrea make enough plays outside of the pocket to keep drives alive and convert in the red zone this weekend? That will make the difference in this one. Nebraska may even find some success on the ground with Jamal Rule , who hasn't scored since Week 3 but leads the team in rushing this season with 5.3 yards per carry. When stakes are high in rivalry games, both teams usually play to their maximum standard, and it comes down to the end. That's where I'm going here. ... Iowa 20, Nebraska 16. No. 20 Florida (-5.5) at Florida State Hummer ( Florida -5.5) : Florida should roll in this game. The Seminoles are 2-1 since firing Mike Norvell, but the offense has struggled, and they were also just blown out, 28-10, by NC State . But … all the advanced data says that this will be a very close game. Like within a point or two. I just don't see that. The Seminoles are super injured, don't have much to play for and are going up against a Gators team with a better overall roster. Give me the Gators to cover. … Florida 27, Florida State 20. Crawford (Florida -5.5) : Did the Seminoles get caught looking ahead to rivalry weekend last week? I was stunned to flip the channel and see NC State with a double-digit lead in the second half at Doak Campbell. That was an embarrassing loss, one that might keep this team out of the postseason unless they find a way to beat the Gators. I don't see it happening if Florida finds some semblance of consistency defensively and gets a few stops early in the matchup. ... Florida 26, Florida State 17. No. 3 Texas (-10.5) at Texas A&M Hummer (Texas -10.5) : Have you seen the Texas A&M offense recently? The Aggies haven't hit double digits in a game since October, and it's not going to get any easier against a top-10 Texas defense. It's a rivalry game. The Aggies will play hard. But this shouldn't be close. The Longhorns win their third straight in this series. … Texas 28, Texas A&M 10. Crawford (Texas -10.5) : Will Muschamp be licking his chops here? His uber-talented defense against a quarterback making his second start? Takeaways should fall into the Longhorns' lap in a game they need to win to stay in the first-round home game conversation in the CFP. They may even get a matchup with Georgia in the SEC Championship Game to further boost the resume. The Aggies have scored two total touchdowns in their last three SEC games. I'd be surprised if they get one on Saturday. ... Texas 24, Texas A&M 6. No. 19 Louisville (-2.5) at Kentucky Hummer ( Louisville -2.5) : That may feel like a strange line given Kentucky 's start to the season. But the Cardinals, winners of seven straight games, are playing excellent football right now. They've got one of the most explosive offenses in college football (fifth nationally in yards per play) and a rushing defense (34th nationally) that's gotten much better throughout the year. Kentucky, on the other hand, has scored an average of just 11.3 points per game over the last three weeks. The Wildcats do have an advantage along the line of scrimmage. But the Cardinals are also just playing better. Give me the hot team. … Louisville 28, Kentucky 24. Crawford (Kentucky +2.5) : I understand why this one's tilted in Louisville's favor by oddsmakers. Kentucky's frail with three straight losses, but this one feels different for Will Stein in his first rival setting with the Wildcats. They're going all-in this week to salvage what's been a better-than-expected campaign in Lexington, and a victory over Louisville should push Kentucky to a Florida-based bowl game. After playing three straight challenging SEC defenses, Kenny Minchey gets a break against an opponent that ranks 10th in the ACC in total yards allowed. ... Kentucky 28, Louisville 27. Michigan at No. 21 Ohio State (-10.5) Hummer (Ohio State -10.5) : This is the first Michigan-Ohio State matchup since 2017 without any real national title or playoff implications. But there's plenty of pressure on both coaches. Kyle Whittingham remains very much on the hot seat. Ryan Day is amid the worst season of his Ohio State coaching career. I think the Buckeyes win. They're the better overall team. But it's going to be ugly. The defenses make plenty of plays. There is some bad offensive football from Michigan. The Buckeyes pull away late. … Ohio State 27, Michigan 10. Crawford (Michigan +10.5) : Admittedly, I have little confidence here that Michigan can generate enough positive plays to eventually get into scoring position against the Buckeyes. However, I know this defense will do everything in its power to keep Michigan in the game and make this one a late sweat for the home team. It's almost unimaginable that Ryan Day could lose five games as the former preseason No. 1 this fall. There's far too much talent on this Ohio State team to be stumbling down the stretch like this regardless of who's playing quarterback. ... Ohio State 17, Michigan 12. South Carolina (-4.5) at Clemson Hummer ( Clemson +4.5) : I'm not sure which one of these fan bases is all that happy entering this one. The Gamecocks have stalled down the stretch. Clemson is as far removed from the national title picture as it has been in 15 years. This is a game South Carolina should win. The Gamecocks are better. Better QB. Better offensive weapons. Comparable defense. But this is also exactly the type of game Clemson gets up for. picks.blurb: From a conference championship appearance, a playoff berth and a straight-up rivalry, there's a lot at stake for No. 15 USC Trojans' season finale vs. the No. 9 UCLA Bruins. Odds may be shifting the Trojans' way but these three factors can guarantee a upset victory. 1. Defense Flusters UCLA Quarterback Madden Iamaleava The Bruins might have Ty Dieffenbach listed as “probable,” but it could be more of a guise to avoid the outcome Florida State had in 2023. For now, Madden Iamaleava, the younger brother of Nico Iamaleava, is expected to start, and the Trojans' defense should be licking its chops. When the sophomore entered the game, he looked hesitant and unprepared. The result was a rough outing, failing to make a complete pass and rushing for negative yards. On top of his depth chart status at the start of the year, Iamaleava has little high school experience to lean on as well. Madden backed up Nico at Warren High (Downey, Calif.) from his freshman to sophomore year. He made a total of 17 appearances during that time, but it was a small sample size. Then in 2023, Madden became the full-time starter. In 13 games, he threw for 3,626 yards, 43 touchdowns and only four interceptions, per MaxPreps. He showed flashes of being a dynamic runner as well, rushing for 305 yards and three scores. A fallout at Warren led to a midseason transfer attempt to Long Beach Poly. Ultimately, Iamaleava did not play his senior year. Plus, the Bruins' offense has already been struggling under Dieffenbach – four interceptions in seven games, two of which came from Dieffenbach against Michigan in Week 12, No. 98 in points per trip inside the opponent’s 40-yard line and a lack of explosive plays despite having an excellent rushing attack. As great as coach Bob Chesney has been this season, it seems like a tall task to have the young Iamaleava ready on Nov. 28. Despite a slow start, USC’s defense came to play against a red-hot Maryland offense. Despite having a low pressure rate of 28 percent, the line was able to record four quarterback hits. The defensive front also disrupted the Terrapins’ run game with four tackles for loss (seven yards). More importantly, the secondary came away with three interceptions. With a lack of an outside threat, USC can focus on bringing the pressure from the interior and a blitzing nickelback. Desman Stephens II and Deven Bryant have done an excellent job leading the middle of the defense, and they will be huge in slowing down the Bruins' lead back, Wayne Knight. Taking all that into consideration, the Trojans defense can come away with three to four sacks and three turnovers in the contest. 2. Another Dominant Day on the Ground for Waymond Jordan and King Miller It appeared that Lincoln Riley was going to fall into old habits when trailing 14-13 to Maryland at halftime – get pass-happy, speed up the momentum and make questionable play calls. Fortunately, the USC offense got gritty with the run game, taking pressure off quarterback Jayden Maiava while providing an easy check-down option and milking the clock. The dynamic duo of Waymond Jordan and King Miller accounted for 140 of USC’s 184 rushing yards. Jordan – 18 carries, 70 yards, two touchdowns – looks healthy as ever, with his quick cuts and strong finishes. Miller – 10 carries for 70 yards – continues to shine as the explosive runner and is a huge plus as an easy pass option. It's also worth noting that Southern Cal is 8-1 when they rush for 100-plus yards and 0-2 when they rush for less than 100 – both of which were on the road. Riley has seemed to grow fond of the 12-personnel look and two-back backfield, which only opens up the passing game when the backfield duo is rolling. He needs to lean on it once again. Going against the Bruins' defense won't be an easy task, as the unit is No. 6 in rushing yards allowed per game (88.5) and No. 4 in yards per rush (2.7), but if USC can sustain drives with the run, they can tire out and punish this defense. With Miller as the lead rusher this time around, the two will combine for 120-plus yards and account for two scores on the day. 3. Double Digit Victory for the USC Trojans USC has won by double digits five times this season. While all five were at home, the Trojans won’t be dealing with the away-game narrative at the Rose Bowl. Similar to the Ohio State game, the defense will keep everything in front of them while flustering a young, backup quarterback. The offense will be willing to play a smash-mouth game while getting the ball to wideout Trent Mosley for explosive plays for a final score of 35-17. away.headline: USC suspends entire marching band from UCLA game over crude sign prank on Bruins campus
away.blurb: "Out of respect for UCLA, and to provide time to reflect on the collective responsibility we share to uphold our university's values, the university and Trojan Marching Band's leadership have decided that the band will not take the field for their traditional pre-game and halftime performances at the Rose Bowl this Saturday." USC pulled its marching band from Saturday's rivalry game at the Rose Bowl following a late-night campus prank at UCLA . Ahead of the Big Ten matchup between No. 15 USC and No. 9 UCLA, officials barred the Trojan Marching Band from its pregame and halftime shows after members allegedly vandalized signage at the Wasserman Football Center. The incident capped off a spirited Tuesday night in Los Angeles. An hour after the latest College Football Playoff rankings dropped, USC held its annual Conquest pep rally featuring a mock fight between the USC and UCLA mascots. The marching band performed and several USC players attended. Head coach Lincoln Riley did not make an appearance. Later that night, according to UCLA's Daily Bruin, band members allegedly crossed town and removed letters from the Wasserman Football Center's exterior sign to spell "ass Football Center." The vandalism left the facility temporarily branded as the "ASS Football Center." USC President Beong-Soo Kim responded Wednesday with a formal apology to UCLA. "This morning, we learned that a portion of UCLA's campus had been vandalized by individual students belonging to the Trojan Marching Band. This conduct runs contrary to USC's values and is unacceptable," Kim wrote in a statement to the Trojan community. "We are cooperating fully with law enforcement and an investigation is underway. Appropriate interim actions will be or have already been taken, and any student ultimately found responsible will be subject to discipline under university policy." The move will sideline hundreds of student musicians for the actions of a few. Kim added that the decision was made jointly with band leadership. "We want to express our deepest apologies to the entire UCLA community. Our rivalry is one of the great traditions in college athletics, and it has always rested on mutual respect. What happened on UCLA's campus last night has no place in this tradition," Kim wrote. A USC spokesperson declined to share details on the damages or disciplinary process, telling Fox News Digital. "The university does not have further comment as the investigation into the matter is ongoing." UCLA offered Fox News Digital a much looser response: "Go Bruins. Beat SC!" The Crosstown Showdown has a long history of rivalry week pranks and campus raids. Every November, USC students wrap the Tommy Trojan statue in duct tape to protect it from blue and gold paint, while UCLA students pull overnight shifts guarding the Bruin Bear statue and hiding it under a wooden box. USC and UCLA kick off Saturday afternoon in Pasadena. No "Tusk" blaring from the sidelines. Send us your thoughts: alejandro.avila@outkick.

The 15th-ranked Trojans (8-3 overall, 5-3 Big Ten) had scored 10 points in the opening quarter, then allowed the Terrapins to come back and put up two touchdowns in the second quarter. Riley and the coaching staff came into the locker room with fiery intent and immediately addressed the concerns over effort and physicality. USC surged in the second half and outscored Maryland 22-7 to win the game, 35-21 . “I wasn’t real happy,” Riley said after the game. “Honestly, I didn’t really care about the scoreboard. I don’t know – we just didn’t play like us. I thought our edge – some of the things I felt like this team has done pretty consistently throughout the year, I just didn’t see that. “But I was confident that they would respond, and they did.” Adjustments have been made to practice this week in an attempt to eliminate any complacency that could show up in this weekend’s important rivalry game against No. 10 UCLA (10-1, 7-1). “We had some crazy practices already,” cornerback Jontez Williams said with a smirk. “I’d just say we’ve been back to what we need to be, for sure. It was a really physical two days.” Riley has also been leaning on the leadership council to help get messages across to the players in important moments. The council has roughly eight players this season, which is a fairly average size compared to past seasons, and it meets with Riley regularly. Tight end Tucker Ashcraft was on the council while playing at Wisconsin, and has now assumed a role with USC’s group. picks.headline: Week 13 college football betting, odds: 3 early bets to make right now, including in Oklahoma-Missouri
picks.blurb: Week 13 college football betting, odds: 3 early bets to make right now, including in Oklahoma-Missouri - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football CFP And Bowl Games Rodgers goes nuclear NFL on Thanksgiving NBA Cup roundup Steelers release Aaron Rodgers MLB free agency updates Corbie Craig Contributing writer Tue, November 24, 2026 at 10:55 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads College football rivalry week is here, and some of the toughest teams to price are the ones making changes this late in the season. Oklahoma has won three straight with Jason Witten calling plays, Minnesota just won after changing its offensive coordinator, and Wisconsin got a big performance from a quarterback who had lost his starting job. There are reasons to believe those offenses are improving, but I want to be careful about how much of last Saturday carries into this week. I'm starting with three unders, looking at the way these teams have been moving the ball and how much work it takes them to score. Here are my three early Week 13 bets. No. 19 Oklahoma at No. 24 Missouri (-1.5, 41.5) Oklahoma has looked better since Witten took over. Quarterback John Mateer has settled down, and the offense is giving its defense a chance to rest. I understand why people would expect more points here. Against Ole Miss, all three of Oklahoma's offensive scoring drives took at least 12 plays, and Isaiah Sategna added a punt-return touchdown, which helped turn a game in which Mateer threw for 111 yards into a 24-17 win. Then against Texas A&M, the Sooners were tied entering the fourth quarter before finishing a 15-play touchdown drive that took more than eight minutes. A later interception set up a one-play touchdown to Sategna, making the final score look a lot more comfortable than the game had been. Witten can keep Mateer in manageable situations, use the running game and keep Missouri's offense off the field. Oklahoma's defense has held Florida and Texas A&M to seven points apiece during this stretch, with Ole Miss scoring 17 between them. Missouri will test it. QB Austin Simmons threw four touchdown passes against Kentucky, and WR Donovan Olugbode caught two of them. I'm more concerned about those receivers creating quick scores than Missouri consistently driving the length of the field. The Tigers also allowed Kentucky into the red zone seven times while giving up only 14 points, so their defense gave up more chances than the final score suggests. I expect Oklahoma to stick with the patient approach that has worked under Witten, while making Simmons put together longer drives to score. Bet: Under 41.5 (-110) Minnesota at Wisconsin (-7.5, 37.5) Wisconsin just scored 42 points at Purdue, so this is a pretty low number to come back and bet under. RB Colton Joseph returned to the starting job and ran for 187 yards, including touchdowns from 32 and 66 yards out. Darrion Dupree broke a long touchdown run, too. Purdue couldn't handle the quarterback run game, and Wisconsin kept going back to it. Minnesota has to do a better job there. The Gophers allowed Northwestern to rush for 196 yards, and Joseph gave Wisconsin a way to turn a missed assignment into a touchdown without throwing the ball. That's the biggest concern with this bet — but I still don't trust Minnesota to score much. P.J. Fleck fired offensive coordinator Greg Harbaugh Jr. after the Penn State loss, and Eric Koehler took over the play-calling against Northwestern. Darius Taylor ran the ball better and two missed field goals hurt, but the Gophers still went into halftime scoreless. Their first touchdown required a fourth-down conversion, and Anthony Smith then forced and recovered a fumble to give Minnesota a short field for its second TD. QB Drake Lindsey made a great throw late to set up the winning field goal, but even with those plays, Minnesota finished with only 20 points. It hasn't scored more than that in any of its past six games. I can give the coaching change some credit without expecting everything to be fixed before a trip to Wisconsin. The Badgers' defense ranks No. 21 in our ratings, and neither offense is in much of a hurry between snaps. If Minnesota can make Joseph and Dupree string together first downs instead of breaking long runs, Wisconsin can move the ball while taking plenty of time off the clock. Bet: Under 37.5 (-110) North Dakota State (-9.5, 39.5) at San José State San José State nearly forced overtime against UNLV, but the offense still had to work awfully hard to get to 22 points. QB Luke Weaver threw 40 passes while the Spartans ran for just 56 yards. They needed a late touchdown pass to Carson Clark to get within a 2-point conversion then couldn't complete the tying attempt. A week earlier, they scored three points at Air Force. We still rank this offense 128th, and I'm not convinced Weaver gets enough help from the running game to keep it moving against North Dakota State. The Bison's defense certainly gave us a reason to hesitate last week. They led Northern Illinois 31-3 before allowing touchdowns on the Huskies' final three possessions. I still put more weight on a defense we rank No. 29, which held Hawai'i to 13 points and UTEP to seven in its previous two games. San José State needs to sustain drives against that group, and its past two games haven't given me much confidence it can. QB Nathan Hayes is coming off a career-high four touchdown passes, but the Bison finished Saturday by adding defensive tackles as blockers and handing the ball to DJ Scott to run out the clock. With North Dakota State favored here, I expect it to lean on the running game if it gets ahead. I'll back its defense to keep San José State from turning this into a game Hayes has to win through the air. Bet: Under 39.5 (+100)

He was ruled out early in weeks until last week, when he was listed as doubtful before ultimately being unavailable against Ole Miss. He was questionable on Friday's report before becoming a game-time decision. Replacement: Although he's the starter at RG on the depth chart, Fodje could also replace E'Marion Harris at right tackle when he returns to the lineup. In the meantime, Heath Ozaeta has been anchoring that RG spot while Fodje has been out. Cornerback Dakoda Fields, who transferred from Oregon this offseason, has been out the last three games, and now, it's four after being listed as questionable until right before kickoff. RB Tory Blaylock: GAME-TIME DECISION Running back Tory Blaylock was also a game-time decision a week (and a day) ago before carrying the ball nine times for 48 yards, averaging 5.3 yards per carry. He's been a regular on the availability report after being banged up since before the season even kicked off, but he has still missed only the opener. He was listed as probable most of this week. Replacement: Freshman Jonathan Hatton Jr. will get touches whether Blaylock is available or not, but he should get even more if Blaylock is on the sidelines. We also had a brief Xavier Robinson sighting last week, so no Blaylock could help Robinson get on the field more. OU, at 6-4, is eyeing a three-game winning streak and just appeared in the CFP rankings for the first time this season after back-to-back ranked wins. A lot of that newfound success is because of a change at offensive coordinator, with tight ends coach Jason Witten replacing Ben Arbuckle, but there's no doubt the Sooners getting healthier is also a major factor. It's not a long list, but there are still a few player statuses to keep an eye on before kickoff. This is the closest we've been in five weeks to seeing Ryan Fodje on the football field. The Ducks haven't turned it over in any of the last three games, and penalties aren't an issue. Basically, the team is playing better and sharper, and Washington usually needs takeaways. Dylan Raiola could have a difficult start, with the Huskies doing a good job of making things uncomfortable and forcing him to settle into the game. However, I think Raiola will find his footing as the afternoon progresses. Oregon has too much offensive talent to stay quiet for four quarters, and I expect the Ducks to make the necessary adjustments to start moving the football more consistently. Washington will remain competitive, but Oregon’s ability to make plays in key situations will ultimately be the difference. The biggest difference in this matchup will be Oregon’s ground game, specifically running back Dierre Hill. away.blurb: A total of eight players appeared on Indiana's Week 12 availability report on Thursday night. Six of those players have already been ruled out for Saturday's contest against the Huskies, and that group includes some key starters. The biggest losses for Indiana come on the offensive side of the ball. RB Turbo Richard and OL Joe Brunner both being unavailable for the second straight week is a tough blow to Indiana's rushing attack. After taking down USC by a score of 27-13 last week, the Indiana Hoosiers are hitting the road in Week 12. Traveling across the country to Seattle, this weekend's tilt against Washington is the furthest road trip of the regular season for IU. For the most part, Indiana has stayed relatively healthy this season. Curt Cignetti has a solid strategy in place to keep his players healthy, which includes prioritizing player recovery, managing practice workloads, and ensuring athletes receive proper rest and conditioning throughout the season. But at the end of the day, this is still football and injuries happen. Heading into Week 12, the Hoosiers are dealing with some injuries to key players that present some challenges against Washington. Indiana Football Week 12 injury report Here's a look at the full availability report for Indiana heading into Week 12: Richard was brought in from Boston College over the offseason to be Indiana's RB1, and he thrived in that role when healthy. Richard has rushed for 745 yards and team-leading 6.6 yards per carry with 6 touchdowns this season. The good news is that Khobie Martin is back after missing the first half of the season with a broken forearm, and he rushed 12 times for 82 yards and a touchdown last week against USC. Lee Beebe Jr. has also been a reliable rushing force this season, and he totaled 71 yards on 16 carries last week against the Trojans. With Richard sidelined, Martin and Beebe figure to share the workload in the Hoosier backfield once again. Brunner is a fifth-year senior who has been a key part of Indiana's offensive line this season. He transferred to Indiana from Wisconsin back in the spring, and brought plenty of experience with him as he appeared in 39 games with 24 starts during his career with the Badgers. Owning a 6'7" 320-pound frame, Brunner started the first nine games of the season at right guard for the Hoosiers. In his absence, redshirt sophomore Austin Liebfried got the starting nod at right guard against USC on Saturday afternoon. He could be expected to continue in that role, but freshman Sam Simpson could also see expanded opportunities. Last week without Richard and Brunner, Indiana ran for 146 yards and 4.2 yards per carry against USC. Washington's run defense isn't the best in the world, as the Huskies rank 10th in the Big Ten by allowing 132.4 rushing yards per game to their opponents. away.blurb: Not only were defensive lineman Bear Alexander, linebacker Jerry Mixon and receiver Iverson Hooks all absent from the report, but the running back duo of Jordon Davison and Dierre Hill Jr. weren’t ruled out off the bat. Both leading running backs were listed as questionable. The Thanksgiving availability report didn’t see any changes on the Oregon side. For Washington, however, two key receivers were upgraded to probable. Below are all of the players listed as out, doubtful, questionable and probable. This is the second of four required injury reports from the Big Ten, which start three days before the game. Oregon’s next injury report is expected on Friday at 5 p.m. PT. Oregon fans still await clarity on the availability of the running back room. On a positive note, neither Davison nor Hill were ruled out of Saturday’s rivalry game. On the other hand, there hasn’t been an indication that they’re fully good to go, likely making it trickier for the Huskies to prep for the run game. With or without the duo, freshman Brandon Smith will likely still get snaps in the backfield after his impressive 121-yard, two-touchdown performance against Michigan State. If Hill and Davison are limited or out, it might provide more carries for Da’Juan Riggs and Simeon Price again. “Yeah, I think they've shown it when their number's been called, whether that's Brandon (Smith), whether that's Dink (Da’Juan Riggs), whether that's Simeon, all those guys that have been able to step out there on the field, go execute your job at a high level,” Oregon coach Dan Lanning said. Washington’s availability report was lengthy in its own right. While five players were ruled out on Wednesday, seven debuted as questionable, with offensive lineman John Mills also probable. Notably, the Huskies, who are already without receiver Christian Moss, saw receivers Dezmen Roebuck and Chris Lawson both listed as questionable on the first injury report. Both moved to probable on Thursday. While Moss hasn’t recorded a stat in 2026 after a two-touchdown season in 2025, the second-year duo of Roebuck and Lawson have combined for nine touchdowns and 1,567 receiving yards this season. Even though Roebuck also appeared as questionable on the first injury report in Week 12 before playing, both of the Huskies' leading receivers being listed certainly comes as a concern if they’re not good to go against the Ducks, although it appears the duo is trending in a positive direction. home.headline: Who won't play for Oregon football vs. Washington? See injury report
home.blurb: Both Jordon Davison and Dierre Hill Jr. were listed as questionable on the Nov. 25 availability report ahead of No. 12 Oregon's 4:30 p.m. PT game Saturday against No. 24 Washington (7-4, 4-4) at Autzen Stadium. With Hill out for almost all of the game against the Spartans, Oregon leaned on freshman Brandon Smith, who had 14 carries for 121 yards and two touchdowns to bring his season total to 369 yards and four scores on 58 carries. It was the first 100-yard rushing game of the season by a Duck. Bear Alexander – The starting defensive tackle's availability against Michigan State was a game-time decision. He played the first half against the Spartans then was on the sideline in street clothes for the second half. He was not on the Ducks' availability report Wednesday. Tony Cumberland – The four-star freshman defensive tackle from Eugene's Willamette High School was injured in an offseason car accident and remains out. "It's a work in progress with him," Oregon defensive line coach Tony Tuioti said Aug. 17. "I don't think it's going to be anything that we'll be able to see him soon. But he's made so much progress. I think the thing that's most important is that we have him with us and just having him in the room brings a smile to all our faces." Jordon Davison – After being ruled out the last three games, the sophomore running back was listed as questionable Wednesday ahead of the Washington game. Davison was injured against Northwestern on Oct. 31 and hasn't played since. Trent Ferguson – The junior left guard is out for the season with a knee injury suffered against Oklahoma State Sept. 12 during his first career start. Aaron Flowers – The starting safety is out for "the foreseeable future" after having surgery on his shoulder, Lanning said Oct. 14. He left the game against USC on Sept. 26 and hasn't played since. Dierre Hill Jr. – The sophomore running back was listed as questionable on Wednesday's availability report. He was injured against Michigan State last week in the first quarter and left the game. Brayden Platt – Lanning announced after the first week of fall camp that the junior inside linebacker was going to miss time with an undisclosed injury and wouldn't put a timetable on his return. picks.blurb: Four Bold Predictions for Oklahoma State Cowboys vs. Arizona State Sun Devils in Week 12 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football CFP And Bowl Games Rodgers goes nuclear NFL on Thanksgiving NBA Cup roundup Steelers release Aaron Rodgers MLB free agency updates Oklahoma State Cowboys head coach Eric Morris. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Matt Postins · Oklahoma State Cowboys On SI Fri, November 20, 2026 at 9:30 PM UTC · 6 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Earlier this week Oklahoma State head coach Eric Morris made it clear his team has something to play for even with the Big 12 title game off the table. He didn't want to hear anything about lower intensity from his Cowboys (6-4, 4-3 in Big 12) as they prepared for a 9:15 p.m. central kickoff against Arizona State (6-4, 4-3) on Saturday. "[That's] such a silly question to ask - what is there left to play? For us, right now, it's building this thing up, and for our players that have fought so hard [finishing this season is important]." The Cowboys are bowl eligible for the first time since 2023. The Sun Devils are bowl eligible for the third year in a row. The winner of this game could end up with a better bowl bid with a victory. As the Cowboys prepare for a late kickoff against the Sun Devils, here are four bold predictions, including the final score. Caleb Hawkins Has 200+ Yards in Total Offense Oklahoma State Cowboys running back Caleb Hawkins. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Arizona State's defense has been better the past few weeks. It's part of the reason the Sun Devils have won three of their last four games. In that span, they've given up fewer than 17 points three times and allowed 27 points to BYU in the one loss. Arizona State has figured some things out and Morris noted that the Sun Devils have stopped the run well of late. The Cowboys have featured Caleb Hawkins in a big way the last five games. He's rushed for 648 yards and five touchdowns and caught 32 passes for 401 yards and three touchdowns. That's 1,049 all-purpose yards in five games. He's second in the country in the category. Oklahoma State wants to feature him. More important, given Drew Mestemaker's shoulder injury, the Cowboys NEED to feature him. He got 26 touches against Texas Tech and had 143 yards without a score. I suspect the Cowboys are going to feed him in the run game early to allow Mestemaker to settle in - I expected him to start - and then get him the ball in space in the pass game once Mestemaker is comfortably. The Cowboys need him to get 200 or more yards in total offense on Saturday. I think he gets it. Broderick Vehrs Plays a Role on Offense Oklahoma State Cowboys quarterback Broderick Vehrs. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect As I just wrote, I expect Drew Mestemaker to start at quarterback. But it doesn't mean that head coach Eric Morris can't use Broderick Vehrs in some way. He's likely gotten some first-team reps this week on the off-chance that Mestemaker can't go. That has given Morris a chance to look at ways to use the true freshman in ways that could lessen Mestemaker's load and reduce his exposure to injury. Morris has gotten creative with the playbook at times. A couple of weeks ago he ran a play-action shovel pass that happened so quickly I'm not sure anyone realized it. There is little Morris can do if Mestemaker gets flushed out of the pocket. But he won't want to use Mestemaker in designed runs. That's where Vehrs can come in handy. He's shown an ability to run the ball in RPO looks that could help throw defenses off in the right circumstance. He has 58 yards rushing on just five carries so there is some explosiveness there. How Morris uses Vehrs will depend on comfort level. But a package that allows him a handful of plays to try and throw off Arizona State's defense would have the added benefit of minimizing Mestemaker's exposure to re-injury. The Cowboys Get a Defensive Touchdown OSU safety Evan Jackson. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect It's time. In fact, it's past time for the Oklahoma State Cowboys to land another defensive touchdown. It's Game 11. It's time for someone to find the end zone the same way safety Evan Jackson did against UCF. Why should the offense have all the fun? But why this week? The Sun Devils moved to true freshman quarterback Jake Fette as the starter three games ago and he's had a similar impact on Arizona State as veteran quarterback Thomas Castelllanos has had on Texas Tech. He's thrown for 623 yards and three touchdowns with no interceptions. He's also rushed for 23 yards. He hasn't committed a turnover ... yet. Fette will be without one of his top wide receivers, Omarion Miller, who has caught 49 passes this season. He played last week against UCF, so Fette hasn't had the chance to play without the team's second-highest producing receiver. That takes away a rock-solid target. The Cowboys will also be looking for redemption defensively after giving up 52 points to the Red Raiders. Remember how Oklahoma State answered after giving up 51 points to Iowa State? The Cowboys allowed 28 points to Kansas State and forced three turnovers. That's the kind of bounce-back I'm expecting from the Cowboys this Saturday. That bounce-back will lead to a turnover that leads to a defensive touchdown. Given his hard work the past two months, I'll take the easy way out and say LaDainian Fields ends up with a pick-six. Score Prediction Oklahoma State Cowboys quarterback Drew Mestemaker. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Oklahoma State 37, Arizona State 33 The Cowboys haven't been great on the road this season. The performances have been uneven and they're 2-3 away from BPS. But Oklahoma State has followed up every loss with a win this season and I think that's what happens on Saturday. I think quarterback Drew Mestemaker plays without restrictions, but that running back Caleb Hawkins ends up being the star of the show. The defense frustrates ASU quarterback Jake Fette just enough to force him into his first significant mistakes of the season. Cowboys kicker Sam Keltner boots a career-long field goal in the thinner air of Tempe. After that, Oklahoma State will fly home for the regular-season finale against Kansas and awaits its bowl game invitation.
